issues.detail: The Greek word 'εἰ' (ei) is a conditional particle ('if'), but the Vietnamese 'Nếu có ai' adds 'có ai' (anyone/someone), which is not present in the Greek text. The Greek simply says 'if [one] desires...'

The Greek 'ορεγεται' (oregetai) and 'επιθυμει' (epithymei) are two distinct verbs meaning 'desires/longs for' and 'wants/desires'. The Vietnamese combines these into a single conceptual flow ('mong muốn... thì ấy là ưa thích') which loses the specific repetition/emphasis of the two distinct Greek verbs.
